keywords: Ball / football / basketball / goal / basket / bat / throw / catch / kick / bounce / player pila, pilae f. Pilā lūdere — play ball. goal; basket; bat: porta, portae f.; canistrum, canistrī n.; clāva, clāvae f. — Modern sport applications of old nouns. throw; catch; kick: jaciō, jacere; excipiō, excipere; pede pulsāre — Pilam mihi jace. — Throw me the ball. Resiliō, resilīre — spring/bounce back. football; basketball: pilā pedibus lūdere; follis canistrīque lūdus — Recorded modern sport vocabulary; the latter is in the Vatican’s public selection. Baba, in sellā sedēns, pilam puerō pede volvit; puer eam pede pulsat, ut potest — Baba, sitting on a chair, rolls the ball to the boy with her foot; the boy kicks it as best he can (Fābula VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae ). necesse est autem lūsor bonus aliter illam collūsōrī longō, aliter brevī mittat — a good player must throw the ball one way to a tall partner and another way to a short one (Sen. Tum Theodōrus patrem quaeritāre coepit: «Ubi es, tata?» «Ecce mē.» — Then Theo started looking for Dad: “Where are you, Dad?” “Here I am.” (Fābula II, Sintra: castellum et puteus).

keywords: Swing (transitive) / swing (intransitive) / playground swing lībrō, lībrāre; oscillō, oscillāre lībrō, lībrāre, lībrāvī, lībrātum — cause to swing, sway or brandish something; transitive. Lewis & Short II.B–C includes suspended movement and the swinging or brandishing of implements and weapons. oscillō, oscillāre — swing oneself / swing to and fro; intransitive. Traupman explicitly records this on pp. 53 and 389; Lewis & Short cites Festus. No unverified perfect or supine is supplied. oscillum, oscillī n. — swing apparatus; recorded by Traupman and Morgan–Owens for a playground swing. Verse locus: Vergil, G. 2.389 oscilla ex altā suspendunt mollia pīnū , which Lewis & Short cites both for the swing and for the little masks hung from trees. impellō, impellere, impulī, impulsum — push or set in motion. Oscillum impelle. — Push the swing; our composed prompt for swinging someone on it. Vīsne oscillāre? — Do you want to swing? Virgam lībrā. — Swing / brandish the rod. For gentle back-and-forth movement of a person, Tē hūc illūc movē. remains the descriptive prompt in our Monkey Tree Game.
